title: feat(geometry): expand DXF blocks (INSERT) on import
body:
## What changed

The DXF reader now expands each `INSERT` of a `BLOCK` into world geometry. Before this PR, an `INSERT` was skipped and counted, and a user `BLOCK` definition stopped the import.

- The reader keeps the text of each block body. At EOF it reads a body once, when an `INSERT` uses it.
- An `INSERT` places its block by `at + R(rotation) S (p - base)`. Z goes by `at_z + sz (z - base_z)`.
- A column and row array (groups 70, 71, 44, 45) places one copy for each cell, along the turned and unscaled block axes.
- Nested blocks compose their transforms.
- A line maps exactly. Under a similarity (equal X and Y scale, any rotation), a circle stays a circle and an arc stays an arc, with exact centre, radius and angles.
- A mirror (one negative scale) reverses the arc: the arc keeps its drawn ends and runs clockwise.
- An exact similarity matrix is needed for the exact circle path. A near similarity takes the ellipse path below (review of the head `87cd87d0e`).
- A SPLINE or ELLIPSE in a block is fitted after its placement, in world units. The body keeps the curve definition, and each placed copy maps it exactly (review of the head `87cd87d0e`).
- Under unequal scales, a circle or an arc becomes an ellipse. The reader lays it with the #3958 ELLIPSE fit: tangent arcs within `CURVE_TOLERANCE_MM` (1 µm, two-sided). The tolerance is recorded on the document.
- Block geometry on layer `0` takes the layer of its `INSERT` (the DXF rule), also through nested inserts. The chainer joins only primitives on the same layer, so this geometry chains with the top-level geometry of that layer. The 2D DXF flow and the wire chain flow need no change.
- TEXT, MTEXT, DIMENSION, HATCH and POINT in a block are skipped and counted, as at top level. Text in a block is not kept as an annotation.

The decision file is `docs/decisions/1865-dxf-insert.md`.

## Bounds and refusals

- Each copy and each placed primitive counts against the vertex limit (`Limits::max_vertices`, 1 000 000 by default). A nested array of empty blocks cannot hang the import.
- An array with more copies than that limit is refused before any work.
- Nesting is bounded by `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH` = 8 levels.
- These are refused by name (the `INSERT` or `BLOCK` name is in the message):
  - a cyclic or self reference;
  - a block that is not defined (before this PR such an `INSERT` was skipped);
  - nesting past 8 levels;
  - an array count below 1;
  - a scale of zero, or a scale outside 1e-9 to 1e9 in size;
  - a non-finite value;
  - an extrusion that is not +Z, a thickness, paper space;
  - an external reference block (flag 4 or 8);
  - a duplicate block name (names ignore case);
  - a `BLOCK` without `ENDBLK`;
  - placed geometry outside the coordinate range;
  - a block whose Z plane differs from the drawing's.
- Bad geometry in a used block is refused with the block name first (`BLOCK A: LINE: zero-length entity`).
- A block that no `INSERT` uses is not read. Thus a bad or cyclic block that is never placed does not stop the import.

## Review fixes (head `87cd87d0e` review)

1. Tolerance after the complete INSERT transform. Before, a block SPLINE or ELLIPSE was fitted in block units, and the placement scaled the fit error. Now a block body keeps each SPLINE and ELLIPSE as its definition (`insert_curve.rs`, new). Each placed copy maps the ellipse centre and axis vectors, or the spline control points, by the affine map of the whole INSERT chain. Then it fits the curve in world units within `CURVE_TOLERANCE_MM`. The reviewer's ELLIPSE (ratio 0.99995, scale 100) now gives tangent arcs within 1 µm of the true ellipse.
2. Similarity shortcut bounded in drawing units. The shortcut to an exact circle now needs an exact matrix (`a == d && b == -c`, or the mirror form). Equal scales give exact entries, also when nested transforms compose them. A near similarity takes the ellipse path, which measures `major - minor` in drawing units against the tolerance and records the tolerance. The reviewer's case (radius 1000, scales 1e8 and 1e8 + 5e-5) is refused by name: `INSERT: curve is too long for its tolerance within the import budget`.

The top-level SPLINE and ELLIPSE paths of #3958 fit in drawing units, with no transform after the fit. The only later scale is the unit scale, and `SketchData::from_document` already refuses a tolerance that the unit makes looser than 1 µm (`sketch_data.rs:115`).

New pinning tests, `dxf` binary, `block_curves` (a new submodule of the existing `dxf` directory suite):
- `a_scaled_near_round_ellipse_keeps_the_bound_in_world_units` (the reviewer's repro)
- `a_nested_scaled_ellipse_keeps_the_bound_in_world_units` (two levels, scale 10 x 10, turned 30 degrees)
- `an_unequally_scaled_ellipse_keeps_the_bound_in_world_units`
- `a_scaled_spline_keeps_the_bound_in_world_units` (equal, unequal and mirrored scales)
- `a_nested_scaled_spline_keeps_the_bound_in_world_units`
- `a_near_similarity_is_no_exact_circle` (the reviewer's repro)
- `a_near_similarity_within_the_tolerance_records_it`

Each test samples 4001 points of the exact affine image of the drawn curve, checks each point within 1 µm (1 % slack) of the output, checks `curve_tolerance == Some(0.001)`, and checks that the pieces join.

Mutations (each undone after the run):
- Block curves not deferred (`defer_curves` kept `false` in `Expansion::body`): 5 tests red (all ellipse and spline tests of `block_curves`).
- The old relative threshold `1e-12 * max|entry|` restored in `Affine::similarity`: `a_near_similarity_is_no_exact_circle` red.
- Before the fix, all 6 first tests were red on `87cd87d0e` (for example 0.05 mm at the minor end of the reviewer's ellipse).

## Readings

- `crates/geometry/src/dxf/insert.rs` (new): `INSERT` record, block definitions, expansion and bounds.
- `crates/geometry/src/dxf/insert_place.rs` (new): the affine map and the placement of one primitive.
- `crates/geometry/src/dxf/insert_curve.rs` (new): block SPLINE and ELLIPSE definitions, placed exactly and fitted after the placement.
- `crates/geometry/src/dxf/nurbs.rs`: `Nurbs::mapped` maps the control points.
- `crates/geometry/src/dxf/curves.rs`: the tail of the ELLIPSE fit is now `ellipse_arcs`, and the SPLINE fit is `spline_arcs`, both shared with the placement. A block body defers its curves. The top-level output does not change.
- `crates/geometry/src/dxf/reader.rs`, `blocks.rs`, `types.rs`, `mod.rs`: the entity loop also reads a block body; non-layout blocks go to the definitions; expansion at EOF.

## Pinning tests

Geometry (`camcraft-geometry`):
- `dxf` binary, `blocks::insert_moves_turns_and_scales_a_block_keeping_arcs_exact`
- `blocks::a_mirrored_insert_reverses_the_arc`
- `blocks::unequal_scale_turns_a_circle_into_tangent_arcs_within_the_bound` (4000 points of the true ellipse within 1 µm; the pieces join end to end)
- `blocks::a_mirrored_unequal_scale_keeps_the_arc_ends`
- `blocks::array_places_columns_and_rows_along_the_turned_axes`
- `blocks::nested_blocks_compose_and_layer_zero_takes_the_insert_layer` (3 levels)
- `blocks::a_block_reference_that_was_skipped_now_reads_its_block`
- `dxf_refusals` binary, `block_refusals::cyclic_missing_and_too_deep_blocks_are_refused_by_name`
- `block_refusals::copy_counts_past_the_vertex_limit_are_refused_without_the_work`
- `block_refusals::bad_insert_and_block_values_are_refused_by_name`
- `block_refusals::mutated_block_records_never_panic` (fixed-seed mutation loop, 300 cases)

App (`camcraft-app`):
- `wire_dxf_selection` binary, `arcs::an_inserted_block_cuts_and_posts_like_the_same_top_level_circle`: a circle in a nested block, inserted at half scale and turned, on layer `0` under an `INSERT` on `outline`. It posts byte for byte the program of the golden `wire-iso/wire_dxf_die_circle.nc` (two G3 blocks with I J).
- `arcs::arcs_stay_refused_for_taper_and_a_hatch_still_blocks_the_cut`: an `INSERT` of a missing block is now refused at import, by name.

Changed tests (old behaviour removed):
- `dxf/curves.rs`: `insert_and_point_are_skipped_and_the_rest_reads` is replaced by `blocks::a_block_reference_that_was_skipped_now_reads_its_block` (the ATTRIB/SEQEND refusal moved to `block_refusals`).
- `dxf_refusals::dxf_unsupported_entities_are_refused_by_name`: an `INSERT` without a block name is refused; an empty user block reads.
- `dxf_inert_sections::layout_wrappers_refuse_geometry_external_content_and_broken_structure`: `Fixture` is a user block now, not a refused layout.

Goldens moved: none.

## Gate (Mac, head `9b384b67f`)

The log is `4052-9b384b67f8b630f2b313a7d55d445cb05202fbfe.log` in the session scratchpad. Its first line is the head SHA `9b384b67f`. The head merges cleanly with `origin/main`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 1217 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (40.5 min). A geometry change falls back to the batch plan, with each test binary. The plan included `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. The app is not changed by the review fix.
- P4: no heavy step.

The earlier gate of the head `87cd87d0e` (Windows) is replaced by this gate.

## Not exercised

- A real CAD file with blocks. The fixtures are hand-built from the DXF Reference.
- `ATTRIB` values are not placed (they are text).
- The UI and MCP surfaces: they read the same `Document`, with no code change.

Changelog: DXF import expands blocks: each INSERT places its block's lines, arcs, circles, splines and ellipses (move, turn, scale, mirror, row/column arrays, nested blocks up to 8 levels). Unequal scales, and splines and ellipses at each placed size, give tangent arcs within 1 µm. Cycles, missing blocks and too many copies are refused by name.

Effort: max
